**David Michael Hasselhoff** (born July 17, 1952),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1) nicknamed "**the Hoff**",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-2) is an American actor, singer, producer, and television personality. He first gained recognition on the soap opera _The Young and the Restless_ (1975–1982), playing the role of Dr. Snapper Foster. His career continued with his leading role as Michael Knight on the crime drama series _Knight Rider_ (1982–1986) and as L.A. County Lifeguard Mitch Buchannon in the drama series _Baywatch_ (1989–2000), the latter of which he also served as an executive producer.

Hasselhoff has appeared in films, including _DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story_ (2004), _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ (2004), _Click_ (2006), _Hop_ (2011), and _Piranha 3DD_ (2012). Before Samuel L. Jackson, Hasselhoff was the first actor to portray the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury in the television film _Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D._ (1998). He made his Broadway debut in the musical _Jekyll & Hyde_ (2000) and went on to star in other musicals including _Chicago_ (2004) and _The Producers_ (2007).
Hasselhoff has released a total of fifteen studio albums, which found success mostly in German-speaking parts of Europe, where he has garnered multiple gold and platinum awards, with the single "Looking for Freedom" reaching number one in Germany and Switzerland. Hasselhoff has also worked as a talent show judge on television shows such as _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ (2006–2009) and _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ (2011).

## Early life and education
Hasselhoff was born in Baltimore, Maryland, the son of Dolores Theresa (née Mullinex), a homemaker, and Joseph Vincent Hasselhoff, a business executive.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3) His family is Roman Catholic with German, English, and Irish descent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-5) His great-great-grandmother, Meta, emigrated with her family to Baltimore from Völkersen, Kingdom of Hanover, in 1865.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-6)
He spent his childhood in Jacksonville, Florida, and later lived in Atlanta, Georgia, where he attended Marist School. Hasselhoff made his theatrical debut at the age of seven in _Peter Pan_, and ever since his childhood dream was to have a career on Broadway.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-7) He graduated from Lyons Township High School in La Grange, Illinois, in 1970.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-8) He was a member of the speech team, senior discussion leaders, president of the choir, captain of the volleyball team and held roles in several plays (including one lead role as Matt in _The Fantasticks_). He studied at Oakland University, then studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts until 1973.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-9)

## Early career
Hasselhoff in costume as Michael Knight in 1986
Hasselhoff portrayed Dr. "Snapper Foster" on _The Young and the Restless_ from 1975 to 1982, leaving the series as the show wrote out many of their original characters. His feature film debut was in 1974 as "Boner" in _Revenge of the Cheerleaders_, which he did to get accredited into the Screen Actors Guild. At the time, he believed that the film would not be released, but it was: two years later, also appearing under the title _Caught with their Pants Down_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-10) In 1979, he played "Simon" in _Starcrash_. He launched his singing career with guest appearances on the first season of children's program _Kids Incorporated_, performing "Do You Love Me". He guest-starred on two episodes of _[Diff'rent Strokes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff'rent\_Strokes "Diff'rent Strokes")_ and the soap opera _Santa Barbara_ as himself in 1984.

## Early career
### _Knight Rider_
Hasselhoff was recruited by then-NBC-president Brandon Tartikoff to star in the actioncrime drama series _Knight Rider_ from 1982 to 1986 as Michael Knight. The actor has described _Knight Rider_ as more than a TV show: "It's a phenomenon. It's bigger than _Baywatch_ ever was." On the success of _Knight Rider_ – "It's because it was about saving lives, not taking lives, and it was how one man really can make a difference."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Khaleej_Times_2006_p419-11)
He describes the acting he has done as "a little more difficult than if you had a regularly well-written script – like, if I was going to be in, say, _Reservoir Dogs_, or _The Godfather_, or _Dances with Wolves_ or _Lawrence of Arabia_ or _ER_ -- I had to talk to a car."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-12) His role in the show led him to win Favorite Male Performer in a New TV Program at the [9th People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_People's_Choice_Awards "9th People's Choice Awards") in 1983.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-13)

## Early career
### _Baywatch_
In 2006, Hasselhoff became a co-judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_, a show that showcases America's best amateur entertainers. He also judged in the [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_2 "America's Got Talent season 2"), [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_3 "America's Got Talent season 3") and [fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_4 "America's Got Talent season 4") seasons alongside Sharon Osbourne and Piers Morgan. On the 2007 season finale, Hasselhoff sang "This Is the Moment". He was replaced by comedian Howie Mandel for [season five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_5 "America's Got Talent season 5").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-20)

## Later career
Hasselhoff produced _Baywatch_ for first run syndication. He has spoken at both the Oxford and Cambridge Student Unions.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-21)
He was a celebrity cast member on the eleventh season of _Dancing with the Stars_ which increased in ratings by 36% from the previous year and served as a judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ from 2006 to 2009. In 2011, he joined the _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ judging panel, as the additional fourth judge for [series 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's_Got_Talent_series_5 "Britain's Got Talent series 5").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-22)
Hasselhoff was later honored on Comedy Central's _The Comedy Central Roast of David Hasselhoff_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-23) in addition to receiving the International Star of the Year Award for Outstanding Contribution to Global Entertainment by the Bollywood Awards.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-24) He was awarded the Comeback Star of the Year award during the [VH1 Big in '06 Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1_Big_in_'06_Awards "VH1 Big in '06 Awards").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-25)
Hasselhoff waving the checkered flag at the 2008 Gumball 3000

## Later career
In February 2008, towards the end of the _Knight Rider 2008_, he reprised his career-making role as Michael Knight as he walked on to introduce himself to his on-screen son, Mike Traceur. On November 12, 2008, he became the first celebrity downloadable character for the PlayStation Network's video game _Pain_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-26)
In September 2009, he featured on a radio podcast for Compare the Meerkat, part of the advertising for British website, Compare the Market.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-27) He was the subject of an Early Day Motion in the House of Commons of the United Kingdom as a result of his support for the re-opening of Morecambe Winter Gardens.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-28)
In 2010, Hasselhoff guest hosted professional wrestling's _WWE Raw_ in London, England. On August 15, 2010, Comedy Central aired a special "roast" of Hasselhoff.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-29)
Hasselhoff returned to _The Young and the Restless_, reprising his role as "Snapper" for a short arc that aired in mid-June 2010.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-30) Hasselhoff appeared as a contestant on season 11 of _Dancing with the Stars_. His professional dance partner was Kym Johnson. On September 21, 2010, they were the first couple eliminated from the competition. Coincidentally, Hasselhoff competed against Brandy Norwood, who judged alongside him in the [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_1 "America's Got Talent season 1") of _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-31)

## Later career
In October 2010, it was announced that he would be playing Captain Hook in the New Wimbledon Theatre production of the pantomime _Peter Pan_ from December 2010 to January 2011.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-32) He has reprised his role of "Hoff the Hook"[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-33) for 2012 at the Manchester Opera House.
In 2011, he was a guest judge at the Belgian Idols competition.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-34) Hasselhoff became a judge on _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ in 2011 alongside Amanda Holden, Michael McIntyre and Simon Cowell. However, Hasselhoff was axed after only one series on the show and was replaced by David Walliams. In 2011, he revived his music career with a short tour across Germany, Austria and Switzerland._[citation needed_] In the same year, Hasselhoff was featured in the trailer of the spin-off downloadable game, _Burnout Crash!_.
On February 24, 2014, he opened his own 10-week talk show in Sweden on TV3, in English.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-35) A similar show was later recorded in Finland, premiering on Sub on April 2, 2015.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-36)

**David Michael Hasselhoff** (born July 17, 1952),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1) nicknamed "**the Hoff**",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-2) is an American actor, singer, producer, and television personality. He first gained recognition on the soap opera _The Young and the Restless_ (1975–1982), playing the role of Dr. Snapper Foster. His career continued with his leading role as Michael Knight on the crime drama series _Knight Rider_ (1982–1986) and as L.A. County Lifeguard Mitch Buchannon in the drama series _Baywatch_ (1989–2000), the latter of which he also served as an executive producer.
texts.1:
Hasselhoff has appeared in films, including _DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story_ (2004), _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ (2004), _Click_ (2006), _Hop_ (2011), and _Piranha 3DD_ (2012). Before Samuel L. Jackson, Hasselhoff was the first actor to portray the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury in the television film _Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D._ (1998). He made his Broadway debut in the musical _Jekyll & Hyde_ (2000) and went on to star in other musicals including _Chicago_ (2004) and _The Producers_ (2007).
Hasselhoff has released a total of fifteen studio albums, which found success mostly in German-speaking parts of Europe, where he has garnered multiple gold and platinum awards, with the single "Looking for Freedom" reaching number one in Germany and Switzerland. Hasselhoff has also worked as a talent show judge on television shows such as _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ (2006–2009) and _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ (2011).
texts.2:
## Early life and education
Hasselhoff was born in Baltimore, Maryland, the son of Dolores Theresa (née Mullinex), a homemaker, and Joseph Vincent Hasselhoff, a business executive.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3) His family is Roman Catholic with German, English, and Irish descent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-5) His great-great-grandmother, Meta, emigrated with her family to Baltimore from Völkersen, Kingdom of Hanover, in 1865.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-6)
He spent his childhood in Jacksonville, Florida, and later lived in Atlanta, Georgia, where he attended Marist School. Hasselhoff made his theatrical debut at the age of seven in _Peter Pan_, and ever since his childhood dream was to have a career on Broadway.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-7) He graduated from Lyons Township High School in La Grange, Illinois, in 1970.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-8) He was a member of the speech team, senior discussion leaders, president of the choir, captain of the volleyball team and held roles in several plays (including one lead role as Matt in _The Fantasticks_). He studied at Oakland University, then studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts until 1973.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-9)
texts.3:
## Early career
Hasselhoff in costume as Michael Knight in 1986
Hasselhoff portrayed Dr. "Snapper Foster" on _The Young and the Restless_ from 1975 to 1982, leaving the series as the show wrote out many of their original characters. His feature film debut was in 1974 as "Boner" in _Revenge of the Cheerleaders_, which he did to get accredited into the Screen Actors Guild. At the time, he believed that the film would not be released, but it was: two years later, also appearing under the title _Caught with their Pants Down_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-10) In 1979, he played "Simon" in _Starcrash_. He launched his singing career with guest appearances on the first season of children's program _Kids Incorporated_, performing "Do You Love Me". He guest-starred on two episodes of _[Diff'rent Strokes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff'rent\_Strokes "Diff'rent Strokes")_ and the soap opera _Santa Barbara_ as himself in 1984.
texts.4:
## Early career
### _Knight Rider_
Hasselhoff was recruited by then-NBC-president Brandon Tartikoff to star in the actioncrime drama series _Knight Rider_ from 1982 to 1986 as Michael Knight. The actor has described _Knight Rider_ as more than a TV show: "It's a phenomenon. It's bigger than _Baywatch_ ever was." On the success of _Knight Rider_ – "It's because it was about saving lives, not taking lives, and it was how one man really can make a difference."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Khaleej_Times_2006_p419-11)
He describes the acting he has done as "a little more difficult than if you had a regularly well-written script – like, if I was going to be in, say, _Reservoir Dogs_, or _The Godfather_, or _Dances with Wolves_ or _Lawrence of Arabia_ or _ER_ -- I had to talk to a car."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-12) His role in the show led him to win Favorite Male Performer in a New TV Program at the [9th People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_People's_Choice_Awards "9th People's Choice Awards") in 1983.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-13)
texts.8:
## Early career
### _Baywatch_
In 2006, Hasselhoff became a co-judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_, a show that showcases America's best amateur entertainers. He also judged in the [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_2 "America's Got Talent season 2"), [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_3 "America's Got Talent season 3") and [fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_4 "America's Got Talent season 4") seasons alongside Sharon Osbourne and Piers Morgan. On the 2007 season finale, Hasselhoff sang "This Is the Moment". He was replaced by comedian Howie Mandel for [season five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_5 "America's Got Talent season 5").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-20)
texts.9:
## Later career
Hasselhoff produced _Baywatch_ for first run syndication. He has spoken at both the Oxford and Cambridge Student Unions.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-21)
He was a celebrity cast member on the eleventh season of _Dancing with the Stars_ which increased in ratings by 36% from the previous year and served as a judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ from 2006 to 2009. In 2011, he joined the _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ judging panel, as the additional fourth judge for [series 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's_Got_Talent_series_5 "Britain's Got Talent series 5").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-22)
Hasselhoff was later honored on Comedy Central's _The Comedy Central Roast of David Hasselhoff_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-23) in addition to receiving the International Star of the Year Award for Outstanding Contribution to Global Entertainment by the Bollywood Awards.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-24) He was awarded the Comeback Star of the Year award during the [VH1 Big in '06 Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1_Big_in_'06_Awards "VH1 Big in '06 Awards").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-25)
Hasselhoff waving the checkered flag at the 2008 Gumball 3000
texts.10:
## Later career
In February 2008, towards the end of the _Knight Rider 2008_, he reprised his career-making role as Michael Knight as he walked on to introduce himself to his on-screen son, Mike Traceur. On November 12, 2008, he became the first celebrity downloadable character for the PlayStation Network's video game _Pain_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-26)
In September 2009, he featured on a radio podcast for Compare the Meerkat, part of the advertising for British website, Compare the Market.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-27) He was the subject of an Early Day Motion in the House of Commons of the United Kingdom as a result of his support for the re-opening of Morecambe Winter Gardens.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-28)
In 2010, Hasselhoff guest hosted professional wrestling's _WWE Raw_ in London, England. On August 15, 2010, Comedy Central aired a special "roast" of Hasselhoff.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-29)
Hasselhoff returned to _The Young and the Restless_, reprising his role as "Snapper" for a short arc that aired in mid-June 2010.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-30) Hasselhoff appeared as a contestant on season 11 of _Dancing with the Stars_. His professional dance partner was Kym Johnson. On September 21, 2010, they were the first couple eliminated from the competition. Coincidentally, Hasselhoff competed against Brandy Norwood, who judged alongside him in the [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_1 "America's Got Talent season 1") of _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-31)
texts.11:
## Later career
In October 2010, it was announced that he would be playing Captain Hook in the New Wimbledon Theatre production of the pantomime _Peter Pan_ from December 2010 to January 2011.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-32) He has reprised his role of "Hoff the Hook"[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-33) for 2012 at the Manchester Opera House.
In 2011, he was a guest judge at the Belgian Idols competition.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-34) Hasselhoff became a judge on _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ in 2011 alongside Amanda Holden, Michael McIntyre and Simon Cowell. However, Hasselhoff was axed after only one series on the show and was replaced by David Walliams. In 2011, he revived his music career with a short tour across Germany, Austria and Switzerland._[citation needed_] In the same year, Hasselhoff was featured in the trailer of the spin-off downloadable game, _Burnout Crash!_.
On February 24, 2014, he opened his own 10-week talk show in Sweden on TV3, in English.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-35) A similar show was later recorded in Finland, premiering on Sub on April 2, 2015.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-36)

# David Hasselhoff to Return to CBS’ _The Young and the Restless_
|New York City|  
April 20, 2010
David Hasselhoff
(© Joseph Marzullo/WENN)
David Hasselhoff will reprise his role as Dr. William “Snapper’ Foster. Jr on the CBS daytime drama _The Young and the Restless_ in June, according to TVGuide.com. He originally played the role from 1975 to 1982.
Hasselhoff starred in the title roles of the Broadway musical _Jekyll & Hyde_ and played Roger DeBris in the Las Vegas production of _The Producers_ and Billy Flynn in the London production of _Chicago_.
Hassellhoff’s television credits include the popular series _Knight Rider, Baywatch, Baywatch Nights_, and _America’s Got Talent_. He is also a recording artist.

**David Michael Hasselhoff** (born July 17, 1952),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1) nicknamed "**the Hoff**",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-2) is an American actor, singer, producer, and television personality. He first gained recognition on the soap opera _The Young and the Restless_ (1975–1982), playing the role of Dr. Snapper Foster. His career continued with his leading role as Michael Knight on the crime drama series _Knight Rider_ (1982–1986) and as L.A. County Lifeguard Mitch Buchannon in the drama series _Baywatch_ (1989–2000), the latter of which he also served as an executive producer.

Hasselhoff has appeared in films, including _DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story_ (2004), _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ (2004), _Click_ (2006), _Hop_ (2011), and _Piranha 3DD_ (2012). Before Samuel L. Jackson, Hasselhoff was the first actor to portray the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury in the television film _Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D._ (1998). He made his Broadway debut in the musical _Jekyll & Hyde_ (2000) and went on to star in other musicals including _Chicago_ (2004) and _The Producers_ (2007).
Hasselhoff has released a total of fifteen studio albums, which found success mostly in German-speaking parts of Europe, where he has garnered multiple gold and platinum awards, with the single "Looking for Freedom" reaching number one in Germany and Switzerland. Hasselhoff has also worked as a talent show judge on television shows such as _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ (2006–2009) and _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ (2011).

## Early life and education
Hasselhoff was born in Baltimore, Maryland, the son of Dolores Theresa (née Mullinex), a homemaker, and Joseph Vincent Hasselhoff, a business executive.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Bio-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3) His family is Roman Catholic with German, English, and Irish descent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-bookref1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-5) His great-great-grandmother, Meta, emigrated with her family to Baltimore from Völkersen, Kingdom of Hanover, in 1865.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-6)
He spent his childhood in Jacksonville, Florida, and later lived in Atlanta, Georgia, where he attended Marist School. Hasselhoff made his theatrical debut at the age of seven in _Peter Pan_, and ever since his childhood dream was to have a career on Broadway.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-7) He graduated from Lyons Township High School in La Grange, Illinois, in 1970.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-8) He was a member of the speech team, senior discussion leaders, president of the choir, captain of the volleyball team and held roles in several plays (including one lead role as Matt in _The Fantasticks_). He studied at Oakland University, then studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts until 1973.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-9)

## Early career
Hasselhoff in costume as Michael Knight in 1986
Hasselhoff portrayed Dr. "Snapper Foster" on _The Young and the Restless_ from 1975 to 1982, leaving the series as the show wrote out many of their original characters. His feature film debut was in 1974 as "Boner" in _Revenge of the Cheerleaders_, which he did to get accredited into the Screen Actors Guild. At the time, he believed that the film would not be released, but it was: two years later, also appearing under the title _Caught with their Pants Down_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-10) In 1979, he played "Simon" in _Starcrash_. He launched his singing career with guest appearances on the first season of children's program _Kids Incorporated_, performing "Do You Love Me". He guest-starred on two episodes of _[Diff'rent Strokes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff'rent\_Strokes "Diff'rent Strokes")_ and the soap opera _Santa Barbara_ as himself in 1984.

## Early career
### _Knight Rider_
Hasselhoff was recruited by then-NBC-president Brandon Tartikoff to star in the actioncrime drama series _Knight Rider_ from 1982 to 1986 as Michael Knight. The actor has described _Knight Rider_ as more than a TV show: "It's a phenomenon. It's bigger than _Baywatch_ ever was." On the success of _Knight Rider_ – "It's because it was about saving lives, not taking lives, and it was how one man really can make a difference."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-Khaleej_Times_2006_p419-11)
He describes the acting he has done as "a little more difficult than if you had a regularly well-written script – like, if I was going to be in, say, _Reservoir Dogs_, or _The Godfather_, or _Dances with Wolves_ or _Lawrence of Arabia_ or _ER_ -- I had to talk to a car."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-12) His role in the show led him to win Favorite Male Performer in a New TV Program at the [9th People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_People's_Choice_Awards "9th People's Choice Awards") in 1983.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-13)

## Early career
### _Baywatch_
In 2006, Hasselhoff became a co-judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_, a show that showcases America's best amateur entertainers. He also judged in the [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_2 "America's Got Talent season 2"), [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_3 "America's Got Talent season 3") and [fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_4 "America's Got Talent season 4") seasons alongside Sharon Osbourne and Piers Morgan. On the 2007 season finale, Hasselhoff sang "This Is the Moment". He was replaced by comedian Howie Mandel for [season five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_5 "America's Got Talent season 5").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-20)

## Later career
Hasselhoff produced _Baywatch_ for first run syndication. He has spoken at both the Oxford and Cambridge Student Unions.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-21)
He was a celebrity cast member on the eleventh season of _Dancing with the Stars_ which increased in ratings by 36% from the previous year and served as a judge on NBC's _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_ from 2006 to 2009. In 2011, he joined the _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ judging panel, as the additional fourth judge for [series 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's_Got_Talent_series_5 "Britain's Got Talent series 5").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-22)
Hasselhoff was later honored on Comedy Central's _The Comedy Central Roast of David Hasselhoff_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-23) in addition to receiving the International Star of the Year Award for Outstanding Contribution to Global Entertainment by the Bollywood Awards.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-24) He was awarded the Comeback Star of the Year award during the [VH1 Big in '06 Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1_Big_in_'06_Awards "VH1 Big in '06 Awards").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-25)
Hasselhoff waving the checkered flag at the 2008 Gumball 3000

## Later career
In February 2008, towards the end of the _Knight Rider 2008_, he reprised his career-making role as Michael Knight as he walked on to introduce himself to his on-screen son, Mike Traceur. On November 12, 2008, he became the first celebrity downloadable character for the PlayStation Network's video game _Pain_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-26)
In September 2009, he featured on a radio podcast for Compare the Meerkat, part of the advertising for British website, Compare the Market.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-27) He was the subject of an Early Day Motion in the House of Commons of the United Kingdom as a result of his support for the re-opening of Morecambe Winter Gardens.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-28)
In 2010, Hasselhoff guest hosted professional wrestling's _WWE Raw_ in London, England. On August 15, 2010, Comedy Central aired a special "roast" of Hasselhoff.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-29)
Hasselhoff returned to _The Young and the Restless_, reprising his role as "Snapper" for a short arc that aired in mid-June 2010.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-30) Hasselhoff appeared as a contestant on season 11 of _Dancing with the Stars_. His professional dance partner was Kym Johnson. On September 21, 2010, they were the first couple eliminated from the competition. Coincidentally, Hasselhoff competed against Brandy Norwood, who judged alongside him in the [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's_Got_Talent_season_1 "America's Got Talent season 1") of _[America's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America's\_Got\_Talent "America's Got Talent")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-31)

## Later career
In October 2010, it was announced that he would be playing Captain Hook in the New Wimbledon Theatre production of the pantomime _Peter Pan_ from December 2010 to January 2011.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-32) He has reprised his role of "Hoff the Hook"[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-33) for 2012 at the Manchester Opera House.
In 2011, he was a guest judge at the Belgian Idols competition.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-34) Hasselhoff became a judge on _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ in 2011 alongside Amanda Holden, Michael McIntyre and Simon Cowell. However, Hasselhoff was axed after only one series on the show and was replaced by David Walliams. In 2011, he revived his music career with a short tour across Germany, Austria and Switzerland._[citation needed_] In the same year, Hasselhoff was featured in the trailer of the spin-off downloadable game, _Burnout Crash!_.
On February 24, 2014, he opened his own 10-week talk show in Sweden on TV3, in English.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-35) A similar show was later recorded in Finland, premiering on Sub on April 2, 2015.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hasselhoff#cite_note-36)
